propositions: The Pass-2/Pass-3 LLM judge exhibits drift across repeated re-runs of the same finding (self-consistency variance), injecting noise into the Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary and threatening the reliability of new routing criteria like R5's asserted_capability_confirmed.

Judge verdicts flip across section-order permutations of the input plan (order sensitivity), with prior research reporting 82.5% pairwise-verdict flips; residual order-sensitivity in the gate's absolute-rubric scoring must be measured before R3 lands new order-exposed criteria.
E6 measures self-consistency and order-stability by re-judging frozen, committed samples (not by circular gold-truth labeling) and gating R5 and R3 on explicit κ≥0.6 and raw-agreement≥0.8 floors.

Experiment A (self-consistency) re-judges N=50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort 3 times each (150 agentic Pass-2 calls) and computes agreement on the decision field; Experiment B (order-shuffle) judges 14 permutable plans (≥3 sections) across 3 distinct section orderings (42 full-gate runs) and computes agreement on the verdict field.
